Organic compounds are carbon compounds, usually containing hydrogen. Carbonates, cyanides, carbides, cyanates and oxides of carbon are classified as inorganic compounds.
Carbon forms four covalent bonds and can bond strongly to itself. Through catenation, it forms long, straight and branched chains and rings.

Organic compounds are useful as biomolecules, pharmaceuticals and synthetic fibres. Hydrocarbons are used as fuels and as feedstock to make products such as plastics, medicines, synthetic fibres, paints and varnishes.
